summary: Reserves three IPv4 unicast address blocks for use in examples in specifications and other documents, so examples do not collide with real networks. The blocks are 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, and 203.0.113.0/24. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: Writers need sample IPv4 addresses for examples. This RFC sets aside three blocks for that purpose to reduce confusion with addresses used for other purposes.

questions: which ipv4 addresses are for documentation
can i use 203.0.113.0/24 on the internet
should documentation addresses appear on the internet
subtitle: Three IPv4 address blocks reserved for examples in documents.

tldr.problem: Examples need IPv4 addresses that will not conflict with addresses assigned for other purposes.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC designates 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/24 for documentation and examples.
tldr.outcome: The blocks should not appear on the public Internet. RFC 5737 updates RFC 1166.

today: RFC 5737 is an Informational document that updates RFC 1166. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 5737.

sections.title: Why Documentation Needs Address Blocks
sections.content:
Using designated address ranges in specifications and other documents reduces the chance of conflicts or confusion with addresses assigned for other purposes. RFC 1166 had reserved the first block, 192.0.2.0/24. The other two blocks were allocated mainly to make examples involving more than one network easier to write.

The RFC notes other documentation ranges, including an IPv6 prefix and example domain names.
sections.plainLanguage: Sample addresses should not accidentally point to a real network. These reserved blocks give writers addresses to use in examples.

sections.title: The Three Documentation Blocks
sections.content: The three blocks are 192.0.2.0/24 (TEST-NET-1), 198.51.100.0/24 (TEST-NET-2) and 203.0.113.0/24 (TEST-NET-3). IANA recorded the allocation in the IPv4 address registry, and no end party is to be assigned these addresses.
sections.plainLanguage: There are three named blocks for documentation: TEST-NET-1, TEST-NET-2 and TEST-NET-3. They are not assigned to an end party.

sections.title: Operational Use and an Older Example Range
sections.content:
Addresses in these blocks should not appear on the public Internet. They are used without coordination with IANA or an Internet registry. Network operators should list them as non-routable address space and add them to packet filters when filters are deployed. The RFC says the blocks are not for local use.

The RFC also notes that 128.66.0.0/16 appeared in examples in the past, but was not reserved for a special purpose. It can be used for regular address assignments with caution. The document says it has no security implications.
sections.plainLanguage: Operators should keep the documentation blocks from appearing on the public Internet. The earlier example range 128.66.0.0/16 was not reserved and may have regular assignments.
